provenance: Repository-authored English coding-agent routing cases; no external text was copied.
prompt_templates: Use the most appropriate focused capability to {request}

skills.name: inspect
requests: locate the files and directories relevant to an unfamiliar request.
find where a named behavior is implemented before proposing changes.
survey the repository structure and identify likely entrypoints.
identify the smallest set of source files needed to understand a feature.
map a user-visible command to the code that handles it.

skills.name: task-decomposition
requests: split a large feature into ordered work items with acceptance checks.
turn a broad request into small tasks with explicit dependencies.
separate a cross-module change into independently verifiable steps.
define a work breakdown that isolates risky changes from routine ones.
convert a long implementation request into a dependency-aware execution sequence.

skills.name: architecture
requests: map module boundaries, dependencies, and invariants for a planned subsystem.
decide where the interface between orchestration and execution should live.
evaluate how major packages should collaborate without circular dependencies.
propose a high-level structure for a feature spanning several modules.
identify ownership boundaries before restructuring a core subsystem.

skills.name: api-design
requests: define a stable callable contract with inputs, outputs, and error modes.
shape a small public interface that can support two implementations.
specify request and response semantics for a new endpoint.
review a public contract for compatibility and versioning risks.
design the caller-facing methods for a reusable module.

skills.name: data-model
requests: check entity relationships and persistence invariants for a new workflow.
review database tables for missing constraints and ownership rules.
define durable records for tasks, attempts, and state transitions.
assess whether the domain entities match the storage schema.
identify normalization and integrity risks in a proposed schema.

skills.name: dependency-audit
requests: check package versions, licenses, and lockfile provenance.
identify vulnerable or unmaintained third-party libraries in the build.
verify that declared packages match the resolved dependency graph.
assess an upgrade for transitive compatibility and licensing risk.
produce an evidence-backed inventory of external libraries.

skills.name: debug
requests: reproduce a deterministic crash and isolate its root cause.
trace why a command fails only after the second invocation.
diagnose an exception from a minimal failing example.
localize a broken behavior before suggesting the smallest fix.
explain why a previously passing request now returns an error.

skills.name: performance
requests: profile a slow execution path and identify the dominant bottleneck.
measure where request latency is spent before optimizing it.
compare CPU, memory, and I/O costs for a hot path.
find the cause of a throughput regression using before and after measurements.
reduce tail latency while preserving a measured baseline.

skills.name: concurrency
requests: analyze races, cancellation, and backpressure in parallel workers.
review shared-state access for deadlocks and unsafe interleavings.
verify that bounded workers stop promptly when their parent is cancelled.
check a queue consumer for ordering and duplicate execution hazards.
harden parallel task scheduling against starvation and leaked goroutines.

skills.name: implementation
requests: build the already specified bounded feature and preserve existing contracts.
add the requested behavior to the identified module with focused tests.
complete a concrete repository change whose design is already approved.
write production code for a small, fully defined capability.
carry an accepted change from failing test to working code.

skills.name: refactor
requests: reorganize tangled code without changing observable behavior.
extract a clearer module while keeping callers compatible.
remove duplication from an implementation under existing tests.
simplify an overgrown class without adding features.
improve code locality while preserving all external semantics.

skills.name: migration
requests: move stored records to a new schema with backward compatibility and rollback.
upgrade persisted data without losing old readers or audit history.
plan a staged format transition with dual-read compatibility.
convert legacy configuration to a new representation safely.
execute a versioned storage change with integrity checks.

skills.name: error-handling
requests: make failure paths explicit, bounded, and actionable for callers.
replace swallowed exceptions with stable classified outcomes.
define retryable versus terminal failure semantics in a module.
improve propagated errors without exposing sensitive details.
ensure partial failures cannot be reported as successful completion.

skills.name: serialization
requests: validate a JSON wire format for schema versions and malformed values.
make encoded records deterministic across platforms and line endings.
review structured message compatibility between two processes.
harden decoding against missing fields and invalid primitive types.
pin a canonical byte representation for hashing and replay.

skills.name: parser
requests: review document decoding for malformed input and provenance fidelity.
choose the correct reader for a file type and preserve typed elements.
fix syntax ingestion without guessing content that could not be read.
verify that source locations survive conversion into structured nodes.
harden an input reader against truncated and adversarial files.

skills.name: cli
requests: improve a command-line flow with clear flags, output, and exit codes.
add a subcommand while preserving scripted behavior and help text.
make terminal errors concise and machine-detectable.
define argument validation for a repository command.
streamline an operator workflow executed from a shell.

skills.name: tests
requests: add focused unit coverage for a specified behavior and its edge cases.
write behavioral checks for an existing module contract.
expand automated coverage around a newly identified boundary.
capture expected outputs for valid and invalid local inputs.
improve deterministic verification of one isolated function.

skills.name: integration-test
requests: verify the real interaction between two modules across their interface.
exercise a database adapter and its caller in one automated scenario.
test a request through the process boundary rather than with mocks.
prove that independently tested packages work together in a realistic path.
add a cross-layer check using actual serialization and persistence.

skills.name: regression
requests: turn a previously observed bug into a durable failing example before fixing it.
preserve the exact case that broke after a recent change.
add protection against recurrence of a fixed production defect.
reproduce an old failure and lock its corrected behavior.
create a test that proves a specific defect cannot return.

skills.name: fuzz
requests: probe a decoder with malformed, boundary, and adversarial inputs.
search automatically for crashing values in a pure function.
generate unusual inputs and retain any minimal counterexample.
stress an input contract beyond hand-written examples.
explore random operation sequences for invariant violations.

skills.name: benchmark
requests: run a fixed-budget comparison and record denominator and environment.
measure two implementations under an identical repeatable workload.
establish a reproducible speed baseline with variance.
quantify an optimization against pinned inputs and limits.
produce comparable throughput results without changing the corpus.

skills.name: lint
requests: run repository style checks and fix only relevant violations.
resolve formatter and static style failures in the changed files.
bring a patch into compliance with configured source rules.
identify code-quality diagnostics emitted by the configured checker.
clean up formatting failures without changing program behavior.

skills.name: type-check
requests: run static typing and compilation checks for affected modules.
find incompatible annotations before runtime.
verify that interfaces satisfy compiler-enforced contracts.
diagnose build-time type errors in a multi-language change.
confirm generic and protocol usage with the configured analyzer.

skills.name: release
requests: prepare a reproducible candidate with pinned inputs and checksums.
assemble verified artifacts for publication without overstating evidence.
check version, changelog, provenance, and acceptance gates before shipping.
produce a publishable candidate only after all required checks pass.
package the current revision with auditable evidence and rollback notes.

skills.name: ci
requests: review automated build workflows for reproducibility and failure visibility.
add a required pipeline check for tests and credential scanning.
diagnose why a hosted build job differs from local execution.
harden continuous build configuration and artifact retention.
verify branch checks, caching, and matrix jobs in automation.

skills.name: docker
requests: validate container configuration, health checks, and resource limits.
diagnose a compose service that starts but never becomes healthy.
review image construction for reproducibility and minimal privileges.
verify safe lifecycle behavior for a containerized dependency stack.
fix networking and volume configuration for a local container environment.

skills.name: wsl
requests: diagnose path and process behavior across Windows and Linux integration.
fix a command that works in PowerShell but fails in the Linux subsystem.
review cross-platform filesystem mounts and executable invocation.
trace networking differences between the host and its Linux environment.
validate path translation and line-ending behavior across operating systems.

skills.name: sandbox
requests: review execution isolation, permissions, and resource limits.
ensure an untrusted command cannot escape its allowed workspace.
validate deny-by-default filesystem and network policy.
harden constrained execution against path traversal and privilege escalation.
test that restricted tools fail closed outside approved capabilities.

skills.name: mcp
requests: review model context protocol server lifecycle and tool schemas.
connect an external tool server with bounded startup and shutdown.
validate discovered tool metadata and untrusted output handling.
diagnose a protocol tool that is advertised but cannot be invoked.
verify timeouts and process cleanup for a stdio tool server.

skills.name: observability
requests: add privacy-safe metrics and logs for an operational path.
define stable diagnostic fields for failures and latency.
make a background workflow measurable without exposing content.
review dashboards and signals for actionable operational coverage.
instrument a module with bounded, allowlisted telemetry.

skills.name: trace
requests: validate OpenTelemetry span parentage and context propagation.
join execution and scorer spans by a stable run identifier.
find a broken distributed span chain across process boundaries.
check required trace attributes and exporter failure behavior.
prove that one workflow appears as a connected span topology.

skills.name: security
requests: assess trust boundaries, authorization, and injection risks.
review a feature for unsafe privilege and data exposure paths.
threat-model an untrusted tool execution flow.
verify authentication and fail-closed access control behavior.
identify exploitable input paths and propose bounded mitigations.

skills.name: secrets
requests: scan the exact change set for credential patterns without printing values.
check whether tokens or private keys entered tracked files.
audit staged content for sensitive authentication material.
verify that configuration examples contain placeholders rather than credentials.
detect leaked access material while redacting every match.

skills.name: incident
requests: triage a production-like outage from logs and telemetry.
preserve evidence and identify a bounded mitigation for an active failure.
classify impact and likely cause during an operational disruption.
coordinate diagnosis of a live degradation without destroying evidence.
summarize timeline, symptoms, and immediate containment for an outage.

skills.name: rollback
requests: plan a reversible return to the last known good revision.
define how to undo a deployment while preserving data and evidence.
prepare an inverse operation for a risky schema rollout.
restore prior behavior without deleting historical artifacts.
write a recovery path that can safely reverse the proposed change.

skills.name: git-history
requests: use commit provenance to distinguish current behavior from stale claims.
find when and why a line changed using repository history.
trace a feature across revisions and identify its introducing change.
compare the current tree with an earlier commit for evidence.
audit authorship and change lineage for a sensitive module.

skills.name: documentation
requests: write concise repository guidance that matches verified behavior.
update user-facing instructions without copying stale design claims.
document a command with prerequisites, examples, and evidence limits.
improve reference text for a newly supported workflow.
replace misleading project prose with accurate current capabilities.

skills.name: review
requests: examine the current change set for concrete bugs and regression risks.
assess a patch against its requirements and repository conventions.
report correctness findings before summarizing a proposed merge.
check modified code for behavioral gaps and missing coverage.
evaluate staged changes and rank actionable defects by severity.

skills.name: commit
requests: draft a conventional change message from the current diff.
summarize staged modifications into a concise version-control message.
propose a clear subject and body for recording this patch.
write the repository history entry that describes the current changes.
turn the verified diff into one conventional revision message.

skills.name: init
requests: bootstrap project instructions and a minimal repository structure.
set up the initial agent configuration for a new codebase.
create the starting files needed to use the coding assistant here.
establish a clean project skeleton and explain its entrypoints.
prepare first-run repository metadata and baseline directories.
